en: The Sūtra on the Body of the Mūla-Dhāraṇī of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Bodhiruci of India during the Tang Dynasty.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara joined his palms in reverent salutation and addressed the World-Honored One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One, saying:
"This is due to the inconceivable causes and conditions of merit and virtue from my previous lives."
Now that I have received this prediction from the World-Honored One,
I wish to give rise within my person to a mind of great compassion for the purpose of delivering and guiding others;
I shall act for the benefit of all sentient beings.
Severing all fetters and bonds and extinguishing the eight fears,
I now wish to proclaim the Mūla-dhāraṇī.
By the power and majesty of this Mūla-dhāraṇī, sentient beings in the final age shall receive its protection.
May all be freed from the causes of suffering and attain the fruits of peace and happiness.
In the final five hundred years after the World-Honored One’s passing,
wherever he may be— in kingdoms, cities, towns, villages, mountain forests, or beneath trees— [may this teaching prevail].
There are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, and other sons and daughters of good family who are constantly able,
throughout the six periods of day and night,
to recite, chant, and uphold according to the Dharma this most supreme dharma-gate of the Mūla-dhāraṇī.
In order to repay the Tathāgata’s kindness through mindfulness,
I shall constantly follow and protect this person without ever abandoning them,
ensuring that no jealous or malevolent spirits can compete to invade, harass, or harm them.
Furthermore, it causes all heavy karmic obstacles from past lives to be extinguished at once;
accordingly, one shall swiftly achieve all various dharma-gates, including dhāraṇīs, divine mantras, maṇḍalas, mudrās, and so forth.
Again he addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One, in the final five hundred years, sentient beings will have heavy defilements and meager merit;
most will be unable to maintain single-minded mindfulness."
Should there be any who uphold this [mantra] and are afflicted by ghosts or spirits,
I now uphold it through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power and sovereign supernormal powers to extensively benefit all sentient beings.
To bring peace and happiness to the devas, asuras,
and others, I shall now proclaim this Mother Dhāraṇī Samaya-gate.
Throughout immeasurable kalpas of the past, I...
I have already personally made offerings to and upheld such dhāraṇī methods.
Furthermore, I have seen that all the Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the past, future, and present,
likewise all rely upon this gateway of the Samaya of the Mūla-dhāraṇī.
They shall attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. Furthermore,
there may be sons or daughters of good family who are able to constantly and single-mindedly recite, read, and uphold this most supreme Dharma-gate of the Mūla-dhāraṇī.
In this present life, this person’s speech is fluent and unhindered;
their wisdom and eloquence are thoroughly penetrating among all the great assemblies of devas and humans.
Among them, it is the foremost;
those who hear it rejoice and all bow their heads in prostration.
In whatever place they are born, they shall always be able to reverently serve and behold the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṅgha.
"Know that the fact that all people believe and accept whatever I say is due to the sovereign power of the majestic spiritual authority (*adhiṣṭhāna*) of all Buddhas, and not my own power.
At that time, the World-Honored One praised the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
Excellent, excellent! That you are able to act thus for the benefit,
welfare, and happiness of all devas, humans, asuras, and others, and for the purification of the path of karma—
now I seal this with the Seal of Wisdom.
"May you never again fall back from these various minds of great loving-kindness, great compassion, and skillful means.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara addressed the Buddha once more, saying:
"Bhagavān, I recall that in the past, during immeasurable kalpas,
when I first upheld this *mūla-dhāraṇī* dharma-gate on Mount Potalaka,
I encountered the Māra King leading his hosts of māras to harass and disturb my Dharma."
So that the mantras and incantations might not achieve success,
I then used this Mātṛ-dhāraṇī to subdue the various māras,
causing them all to retreat and disperse.
One should know that the power of this dhāraṇī is inconceivable.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
out of great compassion, for the sake of bringing benefit, peace, and happiness, [spoke it].
Because he was a celestial being of that time,
he immediately manifested before the Buddha and recited the Great Body Dhāraṇī of the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes, using the Universal Gathering Body Seal at the end.
Namo sarvajñāya. Namo ratnatrayāya. Namo amitābhāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksaṃbuddhāya. Namaḥ.

The trichiliocosm, up to the Heaven of Neither Perception nor Non-perception,
all shook in six ways;
the heavens rained down jeweled flowers that fell in profusion and disorder.
The Akaniṣṭha Heaven and the Mahesvara Heaven trembled and were ill at ease, all filled with great terror; likewise,
all the malevolent yakṣas, rākṣasas, and jealous, malicious spirits were seized with fear.
Suffering great agony and distress, they cried out for their lives;
they ran in the four intermediate directions, not knowing where to go.
At that time, the emanation-body Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva appeared.
He addressed the great assembly and all malevolent spirits and ghosts, saying:
"If any among you do not comply with my mantra but instead oppose it,
I shall cause their limbs and joints to suffer burning affliction and pain, and their bodies to be shattered into pieces."
"You ghosts and spirits should know this mantra:
its power can shatter all mountains and dry up the great oceans;
it can also destroy the armies of the asuras and protect all kingdoms and towns."
It destroys all demonic diseases and spirit-induced illnesses,
as well as the poisons of medicinal herbs, insects, and malevolent persons.
Furthermore, it can subdue the gods of the Heaven of the Thirty-three, causing them all to submit and obey.
At that time, the World-Honored One was in the Great Vajra Joyful Supreme Palace,
together with the Bodhisattva Uṣṇīṣavijayā and an immeasurable assembly of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and kiṃnaras who abide in the Buddha-dharma.
At that time, because they had offered various songs and praises to the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara,
the Bodhisattva addressed the Buddha once more, saying:
"World-Honored One, this mantra is also capable of destroying all sentient beings."
Because it is a vast mountain of obscurations and darkness,
there will be sentient beings who believe in, listen to, read, recite,
and according to the Dharma uphold it, as well as those who behold or hear it.
All the dark obstructions of affliction belonging to those persons shall be completely extinguished.
Furthermore, if there should be anyone who, every morning,
gives rise to a mind of reverence and recites or reads this Mūla-dhāraṇī twenty-one times,
they will always be gathered in, protected, and guarded by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara.
If there is a person who contemplates all great vows and the gateways of the Great Samādhi,
and desires to seek their swift accomplishment,
they should sit alone in a pure, secluded, and tranquil place.
If one contemplates Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva without allowing the mind to wander toward other objects,
and recites this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times each time,
there is no wish that will not be fulfilled.
Furthermore, one will be beloved by all sentient beings;
one shall never fall into any realm of evil or impurity when reborn;
and whether sitting, walking, or standing, one will be able to constantly visualize the Buddha as if he were upon the crown of one's head.
All the accumulated evil karmic offenses of this person, gathered throughout immeasurable hundreds of thousands of koṭis of lifetimes, shall be completely extinguished.
This person shall attain the full lifespan of a thousand-year-turning wheel-turning king and the vast mass of merit thereof.
Furthermore, in every successive birth, one shall always be born simultaneously with Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva into a noble family;
if one constantly holds a full handful of fragrant flowers, [this shall come to pass].
First, scatter [the offerings] before the image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva;
then, those who recite this dhāraṇī twenty-one times will immediately attain the great thousandfold merit and the dharma-nature of great compassion.
That person will gradually attain great power and accomplishment in this world.
If they gaze upon the face of the Bodhisattva three times each day and recite this dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times, [they shall achieve success].
One will swiftly behold the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara manifesting a smiling countenance.
Having seen this, one immediately realizes the Radiance-Illuminating Worldly Samādhi of Mindfulness of the Buddha (Buddhānusmṛti-samādhi) of the first stage, Free from Defilement (vimalā-bhūmi).
At the time of death, it will be as if entering meditative absorption.
In whatever place one is born, one shall attain the knowledge of past lives,
and all karmic obstacles and transgressions shall be completely eliminated.
If one wishes to receive and uphold this dhāraṇī:
One should observe this precept from the first to the fifteenth day of the first, fifth, and ninth months of each year.
During the fast, one should wear clean white clothing and consume the three kinds of pure food before a stūpa containing relics or before an image of the Śākyamuni Buddha.
Smear a square altar measuring four cubits on each side with white sandalwood paste.
Then, take various kinds of flowers and incense;
scatter them within the altar before the Buddha, burn incense, and light lamps.
Having conceived a heart of reverence toward the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
one should recite this dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times every day until the night of the fifteenth.
When Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva comes to enter this maṇḍala,
as soon as that person sees him,
all their obscurations and the grave sins of the five heinous acts will be completely extinguished and eliminated.
Their actions of body, speech, and mind all attain purity. Furthermore,
they successively realize the power of the Buddha-samādhi, the power of the stage of consecration (abhiṣeka),
the power of the stages of the pāramitās, and the power of supreme wisdom.
World-Honored One, when it is time for rain,
one should go to a high vantage point, look up at the sky,
and recite this dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times.
Sweet rain shall fall in season, universally moistening and sufficiently nourishing all things.
If one recites this dhāraṇī over the earth one thousand and eight times,
it can cause the hundred grains to all reach full maturity.
If one recites this dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times at the edge of a dried-up pond, river, or spring, the water will immediately fill it to the brim.
If one recites this dhāraṇī over one's hand seven times, [the same result follows].
One who touches the bodies of all sick people will cause them to recover immediately.
If one gazes upon the face or body of a person who has lost mindfulness,
and recites this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times, that person will regain right mindfulness.
If one beholds the faces of those who are hungry or thirsty and recites this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times,
all signs of hunger and thirst will be entirely eliminated.
If one wishes to establish a boundary within the waters of a pool,
one should transcribe this dhāraṇī according to the ritual rules and fasten it to the top of a banner; thus,
for a hundred yojanas, there shall be no calamities or afflictions.
Thereby, a boundary is established to protect them.
Furthermore, if there are sons or daughters of good family who can constantly recite this dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times every day, [they shall likewise be protected].
The mass of merit of such a person cannot be fully described;
they will attain increasingly noble and exalted status with sovereign power,
and will be loved, cherished, and revered by all people.
Because all that is sought shall be obtained in accordance with one's wishes.
If one desires to subdue the various māras and enemies,
one should recite the Mūla-dhāraṇī mantra over agallochum incense twenty-one times.
Then, recite the mantra once and burn [the substance] once;
when this is completed one hundred and eight times, it shall be eradicated.
If you wish for all human beings not to revile or despise you, [perform this].
Every day, recite the mantra over twenty-one willow twigs and chew them in the mouth;
thus one will immediately gain respect.
For those who wish to attain great eloquence and wisdom for themselves:
Take twelve *liang* of stone chrysanthemum (*śi-chāng-pú*),
pound it into a fine powder, and knead it with clarified butter and honey.
Recite the Mūla-dhāraṇī mantra to cause the three signs to appear.
Regarding the signs such as warmth, smoke, and light:
once these signs have been attained,
one should take seven pills daily, with each pill being the size of a medicinal pellet.
Furthermore, apply it to the heart and ingest it for a full hundred days;
one will immediately attain liberating wisdom and unimpeded eloquence.
Additionally, recite the Mātṛkā-dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times every day.

Because one binds twelve seals to protect the body, first is the Seal of Universal Gathering of the Body, the first of the Seals of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva for the Universal Gathering of the Body: First, stand upright with the body straight, feet together and standing side by side.
The right foot is slightly bent.
First, extend the left hand downward;
its ring finger and middle finger are both bent into the palm.
Extend the little finger, index finger, and thumb,
with the palms facing upward;
then do the same with the right hand.
One should bend the elbows so that they are level with the shoulders,
with the palms facing outward.
If one wishes to subdue the hosts of Māra’s enemies and various non-Buddhists who dwell in the dense forest of false views, and cause them to enter the Right Path;
One should form this mudrā and recite the Mūla-dhāraṇī twenty-one times; one’s wishes will surely be fulfilled.
The mantra is as follows:

*Namo ratnatrayāya* | *Namo āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya* | *Tadyathā* | *Abhate abhate* | *Variate* | *Hili hili svāhā* || The Second Dhāraṇī Mudrā of the Total-Holding Dhāraṇī of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes: This follows the previous body-mudrā; join the palms at the heart.
Interlace the middle, ring, and little fingers such that the left hand presses down upon the right; then,
extend both index fingers straight upward so that their tips touch one another.
Second, extend both thumbs upright to press against the first joints of the index fingers,
keeping the palms slightly open.
If good sons or good daughters perform this mudrā, [the merit shall be as follows].
Immediately upon attaining this, the immeasurable evil karma and karmic obstructions accumulated throughout kalpas of birth and death are extinguished all at once.
One shall, in the future, be reborn in the pure lands of the ten directions.
Now, as for Śākyamuni Buddha...
In the past, when he first sat beneath the Bodhi tree,
he was harassed and disturbed by the various Māra kings;
by forming this mudrā as well, he attained peace and happiness.

3. The Mudrā of Liberation and Meditative Concentration of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes: Third. First, bare the right shoulder, place the right knee on the ground, and join the palms above the crown of the head.
Bend the two middle fingers so that their tips touch each other, and press the two thumbs down upon the second joints of the middle fingers.
All Buddhas of the past likewise fully practiced this dharma-gate using this mudrā.
Because all have attained meditative concentration (*dhyāna*), liberation (*vimokṣa*), and samādhi;
if one constantly forms this seal of concentration (*samādhi-mudrā*) and makes offerings,
one will swiftly behold the meditative concentrations of all Buddhas of the ten directions.
The mantra is:

Tadyathā | Sarvadhāraṇīmaṇḍalāya | Hī hī | Pramodita | Sattvāya | Svāhā. The Fourth Thousand-Eyed Seal Mantra of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes: Stand up with both feet together.
First, with the middle, ring, and little fingers of both hands,
place the backs of the nails against one another;
then, extend the two index fingers vertically so that their tips touch.
Second, place the sides of the two thumbs together,
pressing down upon the second phalanges of the index fingers;
extend the wrists about five inches and position them between the eyebrows.
If one constantly practices this dharma-gate of seals and mantras,
one will gradually attain the vision of the pure and wondrous buddha-lands of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of worlds;
in each and every buddha-land, one will encounter one million four thousand bodhisattvas.
One should act as a companion to those who practice together with them.
However, if one has not yet traversed the gateway of the *samantamukha* (all-encompassing) maṇḍala dharma-gate,
one must by no means reveal this seal-dharma gate to such a person.

The mantra is: Oṃ sarvacakrākarāya dhāraṇī jinadinnaye svāhā. The Fifth: The Seal of the Universal Gathering of the Thousand Arms. The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes. Regarding the Seal of the Universal Gathering of the Thousand Arms: Stand up with both feet together.
First, turn the right palm upward with the five fingers each touching one another;
then, with the left palm...
Press the right palm upward against the chest.
The power of this mudrā can subdue all māras and adversaries throughout the trichiliocosm.
The mantra is as follows:

*Tadyathā:* (1) *parogiti* (2) *sarvaraya* (3) *sarvaduṣṭa* (4) *ugrāya me* (5) *svāhā*. (6) The Seal of the Samādhi of Universal Penetration for the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes, the Sixth: Standing up, place the heels together.
First, with the left hand, extend the five fingers and clasp them together, then bend the elbow forward and open it.
Next, do the same with the right hand,
bending the elbow inward and opening it.
This mudrā enables one to penetrate all samādhis and wisdom-seals,
adorning the eighty-four thousand dharma-gates;
all these dharma-gates are illuminated by this Dharma-light.
Because one perceives *samyaksambodhi*, one employs the Great Body Dharani. 7.

Place the palms together at the heart.
Bend both thumbs and insert them into the palms.
Next, bend both ring fingers and press them against the upper joints of the thumbs.

The Seal for Crushing the Trichiliocosm to Extinguish Transgressions. The Fourteenth: The Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Seal for Crushing the Trichiliocosm to Extinguish Transgressions. Standing up, bend the left arm at the elbow with the left hand.
Slightly spread the fingers forward.
Extend all five fingers straight upward with the palms facing outward and splayed.
Next, using the right thumb...
Lay the palm flat across [the chest].
Form a fist with the four fingers and hold it level above the right ear.
While reciting the Body Mantra, move the index finger back and forth.
If there is one who can daily, at the three periods of the day, bind this mudrā and recite the Mūla-dhāraṇī seven times,
they will be able to extinguish the five heinous crimes, the four grave offenses,
and other such transgressions. Furthermore, they shall give rise to a heart of loving-kindness and compassion toward all sentient beings.
Immediately, all roots of sin will be incinerated;
after this body perishes, one shall again encounter a Buddha.
In that buddha-field, he shall become a wheel-turning sage king (cakravartin).
Furthermore, he will realize a dhāraṇī called the "Samādhi-Wisdom of the Inexhaustible Treasury," and his body will be endowed with twenty-eight marks.
One will manifest no longer suffer from ailments such as those of the eyes or tongue,
nor any other diseases within the body;
all karmic offenses from previous lives will be completely extinguished.
If it is a time of drought, take the seeds of *tila* (black sesame) and mix them with the oil of *priyaṅgu* (barnyard millet) seeds.
Form them into pills and recite the mantra over them one hundred and eight times.
Cast them into a stagnant pool, and a great rain will immediately fall.
If there is excessive rain, one should take rice grains and roast them until they flower.
Then, mixing them with mustard oil to form pills, one should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times and cast them into a stagnant pool of water.
The rain ceased immediately. 15.

The Seal for Subduing the Māras and Enemies of the Three Thousand Great Thousandfold World System of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Fifteenth: Interlace the five fingers with the right hand pressing over the left, and clench them tightly into fists.
Place it upon the crown of one's head and recite the Great Body Mantra;
immediately all enemies will be naturally subdued.
If one performs this rite for twenty-nine nights, [the result will be achieved].
Before the stūpa containing the relics, one should take white sandalwood paste and smear it upon the ground to construct an altar measuring two cubits on each side;
within this, one should scatter flowers of various colors.
Having bathed and purified oneself, one puts on new,
clean garments and holds a censer in hand, burning aloeswood incense.
Sit cross-legged facing east.
Visualize the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes as being upon the crown of your head.
Recite the Great Body Dharani one thousand and eight times.
This is the initial efficacy for attaining the supreme siddhi.
Furthermore, take mustard seeds and black sesame,
grind them together in one place until they form a powder.
Pinch a small amount with three fingers;
recite the mantra once for each toss into the fire, continuing this for seven full days at one thousand and eight repetitions per day.
Thereafter, all that is undertaken will be fully accomplished.
16. The Great and Fearless Seal of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes, the Sixteenth: Stand upright with both feet together.
First, with the right hand, raise it and let the left elbow hang down;
do the same with the left hand.
This should be done regularly before a relic or an image.
One who recites the Mahākāya-dhāraṇī one thousand and eight times will swiftly attain the Samaya-gate of the Fearless Bestowal for Benefiting Sentient Beings.

Furthermore, one should take fennel, white mustard seeds, and *khaḍga* (achillea)— the foreign medicinal name being *śatapuṣpā*— and with these substances, one should [perform the rite] before the Buddha or at the site of the mandala.
Recite the Mahāśarīra Dhāraṇī once for each burning, completing one thousand and eight repetitions.
Furthermore, make offerings of incense and flowers to the dhāraṇī scripture;
all the vows one makes will be fully realized.
If other mantras prove ineffective, by reciting this mantra over them, they will all become efficacious.
If one wishes to solicit a dream:
Then, by reciting this mantra and forming the mudrā to seal the eyes,
one will see the matters one contemplates appear in dreams.
If a person lacks merit such that their endeavors do not harmonize with their goals, [they shall recite it].
If one recites this one hundred and eight times daily for a full seven days,
whatever one seeks shall all be attained.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara...
Again he addressed the Buddha, saying: "World-Honored One,
in the past, at the great Dharma assembly in the ocean palace of the Dragon King Sāgara,
I saw the various dragon hosts undergoing great suffering and affliction."
Reflecting upon the various nāgas and all sentient beings, I desired to preach this Dharma so that they might be freed from suffering and rid of all enmity and harm.
At that time, a nāga maiden presented me with a great cintāmaṇi jewel.
It is worth as much as the Sahā world.
For the sake of seeking this Dharma,
I shall also extensively expound for them this method of the Mūla-dhāraṇī, so that they may be free from all suffering.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Sphaṭika addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"I, too, for the sake of benefiting and protecting this dhāraṇī, shall now proclaim the Thousand-Eyed Seal Dhāraṇī for protection."

17. The Seal and Mantra of the Bodhisattva Vaidūryaprabha. The Seal and Mantra of the Bodhisattva Vaidūryaprabha, Number Seventeen. Vimali (1), Mahāvimali (2), Ugrali (3), Mahograli (4), Hummali (5), Mahāhummali (6), Sahale Jale Tidi (7), Svāhā (8). World-Honored One, if there be any good man or good woman who...
In whatever direction one may travel, should they uphold this Dharma of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Bodhisattva,
I shall constantly follow and protect that person,
ensuring that no māras or their retinues cause them distress or confusion.
If a person faces urgent distress, such as another country invading, or the occurrence of thieves and rebellions, one should take five-colored threads and recite this mantra over them.
For every recitation, make a knot; having completed twenty-one knots, tie them around the left arm.
Furthermore, with the left hand, form a fist with the ring finger, middle finger,
and index finger; press down with the thumb and extend the little finger toward the direction of the enemy.
If one recites the mantra one hundred and eight times,
they will all retreat and disperse, unable to cause harm.
At that time, Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva...
While preaching the Dharma amidst the Snowy Mountains,
he gazed afar and saw that the yakṣas, rākṣasas, and the people of the land were consuming only the flesh and blood of sentient beings and possessed no virtuous intent.
Desiring to benefit and skillfully transform them through expedient means, the Bodhisattva,
by the power of his supernormal faculties, immediately arrived in that land and manifested the body of the Great Subduer of Māras with a thousand hands and a thousand eyes.
I shall now explain the accomplishment of the Mūla-dhāraṇī mudrā.
At that time, the Rākṣasa King came to my presence,
seeking refuge and prostrating himself.
I seal this with the Seal of Accomplishment, whereby one shall immediately attain the Dharma of the Unsurpassed Way. 18.
The Eighteenth: The Seal of Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes. Standing upright with feet together, join the palms at the heart.
Interlace the little fingers with the left hand pressing over the right;
recite the Great Body Dharani twenty-one times.
Through various methods of mental cultivation, one will swiftly attain accomplishment.
If one wishes to rescue sentient beings suffering in the six realms of existence,
one should employ the wheel mudrā:
join the tips of all ten fingers together.
Open the wrists and open the palms,
with each of the ten fingers separated by approximately one cun;
this is that which I constantly circulate through the six realms of existence.
It delivers all sentient beings from their various sufferings and hardships;
by forming this seal, one transmigrates through the various realms of existence so that all sentient beings encountered may be entirely freed from suffering.

19. The Seal of the Attainment of Perfect Enlightenment of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes. The nineteenth [seal]: assuming the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
First, extend the five fingers of the left hand with the palm facing upward and place it upon the left knee.
Next, extend the five fingers of the right hand and,
with the palm facing downward, press it upon the right knee.
This mudrā is identical in principle to the mudrā of cessation (*nirodha-mudrā*).
All Buddhas of the past, future, and present have practiced it together.
By honoring this mudrā, one attains the Bodhi of a Buddha.
This seal can eliminate all karmic obstructions.
If a practitioner of dhyāna cultivates various samādhis but they do not manifest,
they should spend seven days and seven nights in an araṇya.
Recite this dhāraṇī and perform this mudrā.
With a sincere mind day and night, contemplate the Buddha exclusively and perform repentance during the six periods of the day;
you will immediately attain the manifestation of all dharmas and acquire a great mass of merit.
Immeasurable, boundless, and incalculable. 20.

The Seal for Summoning the Thirty-three Heavens. The Twenty-first [Seal] of the Thousand Hands and Thousand Eyes Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva for Summoning the Thirty-three Heavens: First, clench the four fingers of the left hand into a fist.
Next, grasp the left thumb with the right hand as if making a fist,
so that the left thumb protrudes from the "tiger's mouth" (the base of the palm) of the right hand.
Move the index finger of the right hand back and forth.
The mantra is: Oṃ, kucī kucī, kuyari, carī carī, carile, svāhā. This is the seal and the mantra.
If a son or daughter of good family, when about to fall asleep,
should form this seal and recite this mantra—
one recitation and one seal for each repetition— until they have completed one hundred and eight times upon their hearts.
Whatever one desires in one's heart will be fully known and seen within dreams and sleep.
If one constantly performs the mudrās and recitations day after day,
all karmic obstacles and hindrances will be swiftly eliminated.
They shall not lose the mind of enlightenment.
Even in the dreams of their sleep during the dark of night,
these matters will gradually expand and increase, and they shall all attain auspiciousness.

Furthermore, one may even dream that the Tathāgata is beneath the Bodhi tree bestowing upon them the prediction of attaining enlightenment, and that Śakra, Brahmā, and the various devas constantly come to attend and protect them. 21.
The Seal for Summoning the Eight Classes of Devas, Nāgas, and Ghosts of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva. Number Twenty-One: Stand up with feet together.
First, bend the left thumb into the palm;
with the other four fingers, form a fist and place it over the heart.
Next, do the same with the right hand, holding it upright.
Place the right hand beside the right ear and move the index finger back and forth.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo Nigaṇṭhāya (1), namo Ariṣṭabhūtāya (2), svāhā (3); namo Ariṣṭarāya (4), iṃhe iṃhe (5), svāhā (6). If any son or daughter of good family receives, maintains, reads, or recites this seal-mantra:
One will swiftly know the events of seven lifetimes;
the venom of snakes and the toxicity of poisons shall not cause harm;
blades shall not injure one, and kings shall not give rise to anger toward one.
They shall never again suffer the pains of hell for kalpas on end.
If one recites this mantra every day,
it will be able to cause the spirits and deities of the twenty-eight divisions to—
One should come to the side of the person reciting the mantra and sit to listen to the recitation.
If a son or daughter of good family is possessed by a malevolent spirit or ghost,
one should take a white thread and, for every mantra recited, tie a knot— making forty-nine knots in total.
If one ties it around the neck, the illness shall immediately be cured.
If there is an epidemic spreading throughout the kingdom and many people are dying,
one should take one thousand and eight stalks of lotus flowers from the royal garden pond.
Furthermore, by reciting the Lotus Flower mantra once for each casting, one burns them with fire until they are completely consumed; thus, pestilence and epidemics will be immediately eliminated. 22.

The Seal of Liberation: The Twenty-second [Chapter], the Seal of Liberation of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara of a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes. One should sit in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*).
First, with the left hand, join the tips of the middle finger and the thumb together;
turn the palm upward and extend the remaining three fingers, placing them upon the left knee.
Next, do the same with the right hand;
place the palm face down upon the right knee.
While forming this mudrā, recite the Great Body Dharani twenty-one times.
May all their aspirations gradually be fulfilled to their complete satisfaction,
and may all those who suffer affliction attain liberation.
Even if good sons or good daughters have committed the ten evil deeds, the five heinous crimes, and other such offenses;
Suppose the entire land of Jambudvīpa were reduced to dust,
and each single mote of dust represented one great kalpa;
this person has committed as many sins as there are such motes of dust.
Such a person should fall into hell and undergo suffering for kalpas with no prospect of escape;
yet if this person, on the fifteenth day of the waxing moon,
for one day and one night, observes silence and abstains from food before an image of the Śarīra, performs mudrās and recites the mantra one thousand and eight times, [they shall be saved].
All such sufferings of the kalpas as described above shall be completely extinguished;
it is impossible that they would not be extinguished.
World-Honored One, if anyone receives and maintains this seal, [the same shall occur].
It possesses great efficacy that is inconceivable. 23.

The Seal of the Sovereign Spiritual Power of Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, the Twenty-third: Standing upright, first clench the left hand into a fist by grasping the big toe of the right foot as if holding a ball.
Next, grasp the back of the left wrist with the right hand and recite the Great Body Mantra and its mudrā seven times.
By the power of this mudrā and mantra, one shall attain supernatural powers.
Abiding in the stage of non-retrogression until the attainment of Bodhi.
When reciting the mantra, do not allow the sound to escape.
24. The Seal of Sovereign Spiritual Transformation of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Number Twenty-Four. First, with the left hand, take the thumb...
Press the small finger against the nail;
next, do the same with the right hand.
The remaining three fingers are each spread apart and held upright.
Joining the palms together so they touch and placing them upon the crown of the head,
recite the Great Body Mantra one hundred and eight times; then,
like a hidden practitioner or a flying immortal, one will travel with complete mastery.
Please [recite] the Heart-Seal Mantra of the Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara King. This seal is the foremost.
For the Fundamental Seal of Invocation: join the palms with the hollows of the hands empty; move the two index fingers back and forth.
Oṃ aruṇite loke viśaye sarva-śatru-pramardana-kāraya hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. The Sutra of the Mother Dhāraṇī-body of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara with a Thousand Hands and a Thousand Eyes.
